t: This is 60 Dean Street, which the record describes as a publishing address in London. The name most tied to the house is the Purkess family. George Purkess, a nineteenth-century publisher, both lived and died here, and his relatives Henry and Alfred Joseph Purkess, also publishers, lived here too. Edith Simcox lived here as well. She was a British writer, philosopher, trade union activist and feminist. There's little more on record about the building itself, but the address connects a family publishing business with a writer who campaigned for working people.
